line: In 46.9% of random phone check-ins, people's minds were elsewhere.
A monk's friend ate tangerine slices, hardly aware he was eating them.
credit: Thich Nhat Hanh · Miracle of Mindfulness

line: Long ago, Arjuna said: the mind is hard to hold, like wind.
Let attention slip briefly, and not paying attention becomes a habit.
One way back: walking among trees refreshed focus more than city streets.
Sleep matters too: short nights slowly weakened focus, and people barely noticed.
The mind rules the senses. But the breath rules the mind.
credit: Hatha Yoga Pradipika 4.29 · tr. P. Sinh

line: In a trial, four weeks of counting breaths cut mind wandering.
On game day, the Lakers breathed together, then stayed steady in overtime.
So how do we make the mind one-pointed? Ashtanga yoga teaches this.
